events.description: Replication initiates at many origins; the first two regulated steps are loading and activation of the replicative DNA helicase.
At an undisturbed fork, Pol ε is modeled as synthesizing the bulk of the leading strand.
Pol α initiates synthesis of Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand.
Pol δ elongates Okazaki fragments and participates in their maturation; fork enzymes also repair discontinuities on the lagging strand.

roles.description: Its loading and activation are the regulated steps that control initiation.
Bulk leading-strand synthesis at an undisturbed fork (model supported by preponderance of evidence).

constraints.constraint: Initiation must be tightly controlled so the genome is duplicated precisely once per cell cycle.
The Pol ε leading-strand assignment is a model supported by the preponderance of evidence, not an absolute rule; alternative proposals and alternative fork contexts are discussed.
Okazaki fragment synthesis requires initiation before elongation and maturation; these are distinct steps assigned to Pol α and Pol δ respectively.
